answer: The German Wirehaired Pointer, known in Germany as the Deutsch Drahthaar, is a German pointing dog of Griffon type. It is closely related to the other German pointers and stands about 57 to 68 cm at the withers. It is a widely kept hunting breed in its homeland.

body: The breed is closely related to the German Short-haired Pointer, the German Long-haired Pointer and the Large Münsterländer. It was definitively accepted by the Fédération Cynologique Internationale in 1954. It is popular in Germany: from 2010 to 2024 new registrations averaged just over 3000 a year, about 4% of all registrations in the country over that period.

As its name says, the breed has a wire-haired coat, typical of the Griffon type of pointing dog. Its height is listed at about 57 to 68 cm at the withers. The source text gives no further detail on colour or build.
Sources give little detail on temperament. As a pointing dog bred for hunting, it is generally described by breeders as a working gun dog, and individual character can vary.

Sources give little specific detail on care. Hunting breeds of this kind are generally thought to need plenty of daily exercise and a job to do, and a wiry coat usually benefits from occasional grooming.

A 2024 UK study found a median longevity of 13 years for the breed, close to the average of 12.5 for all dogs. The source text names no specific conditions; breed clubs generally recommend health screening of breeding stock and regular veterinary check-ups.

faq.a: Yes. It was definitively accepted in 1954 and is FCI breed number 98 in Group 7, Pointing Dogs.
